Every road leads to a dead end. “Where am I supposed to go?” a Palestinian man cries after Israeli occupation warplanes flattened his house and workshop near the Jordanian Hospital in Gaza City’s Tel al-Hawa neighbourhood. Nothing reached his family for free, he says. Not the tent, not the tarps, not even the water jugs. They paid for all of it, scraping the money together while living in a tent, and now the strike has taken what little they had left. The UN-led Shelter Cluster says Gaza needs around 121,000 tents, 561,000 tarps and 1.7 million mattresses to get through winter, yet as of November 5 there were only about 2,800 tents, 76,000 tarps and fewer than 5,000 mattresses inside the Strip, and not a single emergency shelter kit. More than 150,000 tents are sitting outside Gaza waiting for the Israeli occupation’s approval, and the International Organization for Migration says its shelter kits keep being turned away at the crossings as “dual-use” items. Supplies cover barely 17 percent of winter shelter needs, and Save the Children says winter clothing covers just 1 percent. While families wait for aid that never comes, the airstrikes keep coming. @khaled.sulttan

This year’s olive harvest has been the most violent in recent memory, with settler attacks on Palestinian farmers reaching a new high. But for Masafer Yatta, this is only the latest escalation in a decades-long campaign by the Israeli state to expel Palestinians from their land by any means necessary. Working in coordination with the army and police, nearby settlers wage a ceaseless battle against the Palestinians living in this area. Professor Ilan Pappé describes what has been happening to Masafer Yatta since the 1970’s as “incremental colonization, ethnic cleansing, and oppression,” and to be here is to see it firsthand. But the people of Masafer Yatta have earned a reputation for themselves for their resistance to state and settler terror. They simply refuse to leave, and the Israelis simply won’t stop trying to force them to. The Nakba never ended. We’re just watching its latest act.

North Bergen raised the Palestinian flag outside Town Hall for the 10th year on Friday, Nov. 13, at an event organized by the New Jersey chapter of American Muslims for Palestine. "It's important for us to honor every community, every culture. That's what North Bergen is about. Unity," Mayor Hugo Cabrera said. Cabrera said he hopes for peace and solidarity around the world. "What they're going through right now is horrible, and hopefully the future can get a little brighter for them," Cabrera said. North Bergen resident Bader Risheg thanked Cabrera and the Board of Commissioners for supporting the annual flag raising. "All we're asking for is just the same as everyone else, it's equality," Risheg said. "Hopefully one day, sooner than later, that there'll be a free Palestine and that they'll receive the same dignity and humanity that we want here in America."

Some lands are known for their beauty, others for their history. But Palestine carries a story that stretches far beyond its borders, a story written in ancient streets, olive trees and generations of people who call it home. This is Palestine! Welcome to Palestine! 🇵🇸❤️ Located in the Middle East, Palestine consists of two territories: the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, along the eastern Mediterranean. In Bethlehem, the birthplace of Jesus, the ancient Church of the Nativity stands as one of Christianity's most important historic sites. Then there's Jericho, one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities, where thousands of years of human history can still be felt. In Nablus, traditional markets, historic architecture and the famous Palestinian knafeh reveal a culture rich in flavour and tradition. And in Battir, ancient stone terraces, olive groves and beautiful landscapes tell the story of generations connected to the land. But Palestine is more than ancient buildings and beautiful scenery. It is a place of deep cultural traditions, distinctive embroidery, traditional music, delicious food and remarkable hospitality. From its historic cities to its Mediterranean coastline, Palestine carries a heritage that deserves to be discovered and remembered. So, if you could experience one place in Palestine, where would you go? Drop the Palestinian flag in the comments, and follow Travel Scope for more incredible stories from around the world! #Palestine #FreePalestine #Gaza #VisitPalestine #PalestinianCulture

Displaced again and again. Unsafe, dangerous shelter should not be the only option. The world should never accept this. When the first major winter storm swept through Gaza, families who lost their tents took refuge under what was left of bombed buildings. Imagine trying to keep your children dry beneath cracked slabs of concrete and exposed steel, knowing the structure could collapse while you sleep. Buildings already damaged by occupation’s bombardment collapsed during last week’s rains. After three years of destruction, families are still being left to find shelter among the ruins of their neighborhoods. A durable, weatherproof tent can cost up to $700. Donate to The Sameer Project’s General Fund to help us get more families under shelter before the next storm. It’s going to be a long winter.
